authors: Martin Quensen, Mareike Hetzel, Luis Santos, Augusto Smerzi, Géza Tóth, Luca Pezzè, Carsten Klempt
name: luh-data-suporting-publication-hong-ou-mandel-interference-of-more-than-10-indistinguishable-atoms
notes:
The csv files starting with "Figure" or "Extended_Data_Figure" contain the data displayed in the figures.
The file "data_all.csv" contains the data from all experimental repetitions that contribute to the data presented in the manuscript, labelled by "image number".
The main measurement series is organized in seven measurement scenarios, described in extended data figure 1, which differ by the applied Rabi pulse sequence for mode coupling after TMSV creation:
* 1: no Rabi pulses (Twin-Fock states; not used in the manuscript except for the histograms of non-quantized data)
* 2: two pi-pulses, but no coupling pulse (Twin-Fock states)
* 3-6: small rotations, i.e. short coupling pulses
* 7: pi/2-pulse for mode coupling, i.e. HOM coupling (Holland-Burnett states)
title: Data suporting publication 'Hong-Ou-Mandel interference of more than ten indistinguishable atoms'

resources.description:
Camera image evaluation results for 7 x 3816 repetitions of the seven measurement scenarios presented in the manuscript (see extended data figure 1).

Each line contains:
* image number
* measurement scenario number
* camera count value mF=+1, after subtraction of systematic effects
* camera count value mF=0, raw values
* camera count value mF=-1, after subtraction of systematic effects
* quantized atom number mF=+1
* quantized atom number mF=0
* quantized atom number mF=-1
* camera count value mF=+1, raw values
* camera count value mF=+1, raw values

Note that for the mF=+/-1 camera count values two systematic effects were subtracted ('signal leakage' from mF=0 atoms and a drifting background value), as described in the Methods section. This is why the values are non-integers.
resources.name: CCD_image_evaluation_results.csv

resources.description:
Random sampled occurrence data for the uncertainty estimation of the entanglement depth values k.
The underlying probability distributions are multinomial distributions of the Jz values, with the size being the sample number, and the probabilities being the measured frequencies.
Each line contains a random sample of the Twin-Fock state Jz occurrences, and the HB state Jz occurrences (Jx of TF). These samples are used to determine a value k, either by the novel criterion based on parity or by the "old one" based on the variance of Jz. The k values in the manuscript are the mean values, where the displayed error bars are given by asymmetric standard deviations of these k-value samples (see Methods).
resources.name: randomsampled_occurrence_data_for_entanglement_depth_calculation.zip
